$about: Known failing feature/layer pairs of LatexFeatureCoverageTests. A listed layer that still fails is recorded as known-gap; a listed layer that passes fails the test (gap closed — remove it). Keys starting with $ are comments. Grouped by root cause.
cite.cite-thebibliography/api.import: import: the parser emits ImportBibliographyEntry per \bibitem, but LatexImportJobExecutor.MapImportElementToBlock has no case for it, so each \bibitem becomes an empty paragraph block and the document's bibliography stays empty; should become BibliographyEntries (the finalize step creates them only from a .bib in a zip)
cite.cite-thebibliography/api.roundtrip: roundtrip: the empty paragraph blocks the \bibitems became are not exported, so the re-import has fewer blocks (follows from the import gap)

cite.cite-with-note/api.export: \cite[p.~5]{knuth} imports as \cite{knuth}: the parser keeps only the key and drops the optional note (the editor's citation node has no locator field)
figures.includegraphics/api.import: a bare \includegraphics outside a figure environment imports as a paragraph holding the file name ("plot.png"); should be a figure block
figures.includegraphics/api.export: follows from the import gap: exported as the text "plot.png", no \includegraphics
figures.float-caption-label/api.import: the figure's \label{fig:carbon} is dropped: ImportImage has no Label and the parser does not capture it (figure block content supports label)
figures.float-caption-label/api.export: no \label{fig:carbon} in the export (follows from the import gap), so \ref{fig:carbon} is undefined
figures.subfigure/api.import: only the first subfigure survives: the parser takes the first \includegraphics/\caption of the figure and drops b.png, "Right" and the outer caption "Both"
figures.subfigure/api.export: follows from the import gap: only a.png / "Left" exported
figures.float-caption-label/api.typst: typst: an image that was not uploaded fails the whole Typst compile ("file not found … plot.png"); the LaTeX export draws a [Missing figure] box instead — Typst should degrade the same way
figures.subfigure/api.typst: typst: an image that was not uploaded fails the whole Typst compile ("file not found … plot.png"); the LaTeX export draws a [Missing figure] box instead — Typst should degrade the same way
lists.nested/api.import: a nested enumerate is flattened into the parent's items with the environment name leaking as text ("Fruit\nenumerate", "Apple", …); the list model supports items[].children
lists.nested/api.export: follows from the import gap: one flat itemize with "enumerate" printed
lists.description/api.import: description terms are dropped: items are ["The top layer.", "Below it."] with no kind="description"; the list model supports kind=description and items[].description
lists.description/api.export: follows from the import gap: exported as itemize without the \item[Soil] terms
lists.enumitem-label/api.import: enumerate[label=(\alph*)] loses its label format; the list model has labelFormat="alpha" and the exporter writes it back
lists.enumitem-label/api.export: follows from the import gap: plain enumerate
lists.custom-item-label/api.export: \item[$\star$] / \item[--] labels are dropped; the list model has no per-item label, so the export uses default bullets
text.color/api.import: \textcolor{red}{red} imports as "red{red}": the generic command flattener takes the first argument. The editor's colour mark serialises exactly as \textcolor{c}{text} and the exporter reads it; keeping it needs a catalog row for textcolor (CatalogIntegrityTests) — not done here
text.color/api.export: follows from the import gap: "red\{red\}" printed
text.color/api.roundtrip: the stray braces are escaped on export, so the re-import reads "red\{red\}"
text.font-size/api.import: {\small small} imports as "{ small}": the bare size switch is stripped and the group braces stay. The editor's size mark is the {\small …} group, but keeping it breaks nested formatting ({\Huge \textbf{x}} would export literal **), so it needs the exporter to format the group's content first
text.font-size/api.export: follows from the import gap: "\{ small\}" printed
text.font-size/api.roundtrip: the stray braces are escaped on export and re-import as "\{ small\}"
text.accents/api.import: accent macros are not decoded: Caf\'e stays as the literal text "Caf\'e" instead of "Café"
text.accents/api.export: follows from the import gap: exported as "Caf\textbackslash{}'e"
text.nbsp-linebreak/api.export:
\\ inside a paragraph is flattened to a space on import; the editor has a hard-break (
) mark, so the line break is lost
text.nested-formatting/api.export: exporter: the bold rule \*\*([^*]+)\*\* cannot contain a nested *italic*, so "**bold and *italic***" is printed as literal asterisks
layout.spacing/api.import: \vspace{1em} / \hspace{2em} are flattened to their argument, leaking "1em" / "2em" into the text ("Before.1em", "After2emgap.")
layout.hrule/api.export: follows from the import gap (printed "\textbackslash{}noindent0.4pt"); the block model has no rule/divider the LaTeX export writes
advanced.marginpar-todo/api.export: \marginpar{A margin note.} is flattened into the running text ("Main text.A margin note."); the editor has no margin note, so a footnote would be the nearest faithful mapping
advanced.input-include/api.export: \input{chapter1} (file absent) stays in the paragraph as raw text and is exported escaped ("\textbackslash{}input\{chapter1\}" printed); should be dropped with an import warning
advanced.text-macro/api.import: a text macro invocation (\lilia{} / \ours{}) is flattened to its empty argument and disappears ("We use daily."); the definition does reach the custom preamble, so keeping the invocation raw — or expanding it — would be faithful
advanced.text-macro/api.export: follows from the import gap: the macro's text is missing from the export
advanced.def/api.import: a text macro invocation (\lilia{} / \ours{}) is flattened to its empty argument and disappears ("We use daily."); the definition does reach the custom preamble, so keeping the invocation raw — or expanding it — would be faithful
advanced.def/api.export: follows from the import gap: the macro's text is missing from the export
math.declaremathoperator/api.compile: the exported preamble loads the physics package, which already defines \Tr, so the imported \DeclareMathOperator{\Tr}{Tr} fails: "Command \Tr already defined"
math.declaremathoperator/api.typst: typst: \Tr (a user-declared operator) is not translated ("unknown variable: Tr"); the Typst path ignores the custom preamble
structure.chapter/api.import: \chapter is not a sectioning command to the parser (catalog: chapter 'partial'): "Background" lands in the paragraph text
structure.chapter/api.export: follows from the import gap; the exporter also has no chapter level (level 1 is \section)
structure.tableofcontents/api.import: \tableofcontents is stripped by the parser; the tableOfContents block exists and the exporter writes it
structure.appendix/api.export: \appendix is stripped; the block model has no appendix marker, so the appendix sections export as ordinary sections
layout.newpage/api.import: \newpage / \clearpage are stripped by the parser; the pageBreak block exists and the executor maps ImportPageBreak
layout.center/api.export: center / flushright are pass-through environments: the text survives but alignment is lost; the paragraph model has no alignment the LaTeX export writes
tables.tabular/api.export: column alignment is lost: {lcr} imports without columnAlign and exports as {lll}
tables.hlines/api.export: column alignment/rules are lost: {|l|r|} exports as {ll} (booktabs rules)
tables.multicolumn/api.export: \multicolumn{2}{c}{Merged} is flattened to one cell: the header row has 2 cells over 3 columns and the table exports as 2 columns, dropping the cell "3"; the table model supports colspan
tables.multicolumn/api.roundtrip: the export dropped the third column, so the re-import has rows [[1,2]]
tables.multirow/api.export: \multirow{2}{*}{Tall} is flattened to a plain cell; the table model supports rowspan
tables.paragraph-column/api.import: a one-row tabular is taken as header-less and gets invented headers "Column 1", "Column 2"; p{3cm} width is lost
tables.paragraph-column/api.export: the invented "Column 1 / Column 2" header row is exported as a real row
tables.tabularx/api.import: same as tables.paragraph-column: a one-row tabularx gets invented "Column 1 / Column 2" headers
tables.tabularx/api.export: the invented header row is exported
tables.longtable/api.export: longtable imports as an ordinary table (no longTable flag) and exports as a table float
tables.math-in-cells/api.export: exporter: table cells go through EscapeLatex, so $x^2$ in a cell prints as "\$x\textasciicircum{}2\$"; cells should get the inline formatter (math, bold …)
tables.math-in-cells/api.roundtrip: the escaped cells re-import as literal "\$x\$"
advanced.tikz/api.export: PRODUCT DECISION. The import pipeline maps a raw passthrough to a code block (language latex), which the LaTeX export wraps in lstlisting: the source is printed as a listing instead of being typeset. The parser's own comment and telemetry say it should be the embed block (engine latex, exported verbatim), and /api/convert/latex-to-blocks already emits embed
advanced.tikz/api.roundtrip: the lstlisting re-imports as a code block with language "tex" instead of "latex" (follows from the passthrough decision)
